title: The audit's integration-tier gate runs REAL-tmux tests inside a concurrent fleet lane, so tmux contention produces boot-timeout false REDs — cycle-1530 was killed with a SYSTEM-failure halt by 13 offenders that all pass cleanly at the same commit outside the lane
summary: Live, cycle-1530 (wave batch-20260820a-verify). The cycle FAILED with SystemFailure{category: infra-systemic, level: system} and the wave closed on stop_reason=system_failure_halt, 1/2 lanes ok. The orchestrator's own evidence line states the case precisely: 'acs-verdict.json red_count=0 (5/5 behavioral, blocking_count=0) and audit-report.md records a WARN narrative with 0 CRITICAL/HIGH; the only FAIL source is audit-fail-reason.json reasons[0], the integration-tier gate, whose 13 offenders are all bridge REPL tests failing at BOOT'. Every offender is exit=80 (ExitREPLBootTimeout) in tmux_repl_interactive_test.go — e.g. TestRealTmux_Interactive_AgyPermission_AutoYes, _CodexTrust_AutoRespondAtBoot, _Escalate_FailsFastWithReport. VERIFIED FALSE RED: at the identical commit (19b427c4), in an uncontended console environment, `go test -tags integration ./internal/bridge/ -count=1` returns ok with 0 failures in 33s, and the two named offenders pass in 6s. The gate turned a WARN-narrative, red_count=0 cycle into a system-level halt.
root_cause: These are REAL-tmux tests: they spawn their own tmux sessions against a live server (requireTmux, itSession, itTmuxCtl.KillSession) with a 250ms poll interval, and they assert on boot-marker detection timing. The audit's CI-parity integration-tier gate executes them INSIDE a cycle worktree while the fleet is running other lanes that are themselves driving real tmux sessions for their phase agents. Under that contention the boot poll misses its window and every affected test reports exit=80. The gate is CI-parity by intent, but CI runs the integration tier on a dedicated runner with no concurrent tmux load — so the in-lane execution is not parity, it is a strictly harsher and timing-dependent environment.
fix: SUPERSEDES the earlier prescription — three things were learned by attempting it (branch fix/integration-tier-tmux-contention, opus review BLOCK). (1) An env-based skip is DEAD: the gate runs the tier through scrubbedRun, whose integrationTierEnvAllowlist (ciparity.go:373-376) keeps only PATH/HOME/TMPDIR/USER/SHELL/GO*, so any EVOLVE_* probe is a no-op that still passes its own fixtures. (2) 'Add serialization' ALREADY EXISTS and is insufficient: acquireTierLock (ciparity.go:343) serializes a red retake, and cycle-1530's integration-tier.log records '(serialized retake)' with NO lock-wait-timeout note — the lock was acquired and it STILL failed, because the contention is phase-agent tmux load, which holds no tier lock and is not test load. (3) A naive `tmux ls` probe is ALSO a no-op: bridge sessions never live on the DEFAULT socket. Every bridge tmux call goes through TmuxSocketArgs -> -L <socket> (tmux.go:127-133) where the socket is the shared TmuxSocket='evolve-bridge' (tmux.go:97) or a per-run 'evolve-bridge-p<looppid>' (DeriveRunSocket, tmux.go:106-110). Verified on this machine: default socket empty, four live bridge sockets present. Any detection MUST enumerate bridge sockets and query each with -L. RESOLVED UNKNOWN: CI does run this subset — go.yml:65 runs `-tags integration` and CI's internal/bridge line is 49.2s vs 14.3s for the non-integration step (34.1s locally with real-tmux). So making the subset CI-only preserves coverage. REMAINING DESIGN FORK for whoever takes this: (a) runtime socket detection in requireTmux, or (b) a dedicated build tag (e.g. //go:build integration && realtmux) that the in-lane gate omits and go.yml adds — cleaner and greppable, but the real-tmux tests share files with helpers, so it needs file surgery. NOTE either way the outcome is the same and must be STATED, not emergent: with fleet.count>=2 sibling phase agents are live for nearly the whole audit window, so correct detection means this subset effectively NEVER runs in-lane again. Also required: the skip must leave EVIDENCE — the tier runs without -v, so an all-skipped package prints 'ok' and a t.Skipf string reaches no artifact; use the tier's existing WARN channel (ciparity.go:354-362) rather than going silent. Smaller musts: bridgeSessionPrefix must derive from the real const (TmuxSocket+"-") not a copied literal; exec_integration_test.go:75 mints 'evolve-bridge-covtest-<pid>' in the same package and is a self-detection hole; bound the tmux probe with a context timeout and sync.Once.
files: go/internal/phases/audit/ (the CI-parity integration-tier gate that runs them in-lane)
acceptance: A cycle whose only FAIL source is an exit=80-only integration-tier offender set does not escalate to a system-failure halt.
A genuine integration-tier assertion failure still forces FAIL (no gate weakening).
The real-tmux subset either does not run in-lane, or runs serialized, or requires repetition before forcing FAIL — pick one and state it.
connects_to: CLAUDE.md ship-gate rule: 'if a gate reports RED, verify the gate's own logic before assuming the code is broken (false-RED gates have shipped before)' — this is that class
ADR-0072 SYSTEM-fail halt policy (what this false RED triggered)
PR #474 (the change under verification when this fired — cleared: the same tier is green at the same commit outside the lane)
notes: Filed after ruling out the obvious suspect. PR #474 had just merged and touched the bridge REPL driver plus three integration-tagged harnesses, so a regression there was the first hypothesis; it was tested directly rather than argued — full integration tier at the same commit, uncontended: ok, 0 failures. The orchestrator had independently reached the same classification (infra-systemic), which is the gate's saving grace: it named the category correctly even while halting on it. ATTEMPT 1 BLOCKED (recorded so it is not repeated): the guard queried the DEFAULT tmux socket and my wiring proof created its fake session there too — so the proof passed against a server real sessions never use, and the guard would have been a production no-op. The lesson is the session's recurring one, committed inside the very proof meant to prevent it: establish WHERE a signal is durably written before treating its presence or absence as evidence.
